children: SYDNEY--Australia's NextDC has begun a comprehensive capital-expenditure review and could sell some development sites after its near-term earnings outlook was hit by a power-supply delay to one of its Melbourne data centers.
ASX-listed NextDC on Wednesday said it had paused all projects not backed by customer contracts and reallocated capital to building out capacity already contracted to customers.

NextDC cut its guidance for the 12 months through June 30 to reflect the removal of 140 million Australian dollars, or US$98 million, of revenue it had expected to generate from M3 capacity already contracted out to a major customer.
NextDC, which is in the midst of an aggressive expansion in Australia and the Asia-Pacific region, said it was considering whether it could declare force majeure under its M3 contracts.

The company said electricity distributor Jemena suspended power line works in September amid safety concerns and opposition from local residents, who had blocked access to the site. Jemena does not expect to resume work before February, NextDC said.
